currentContext.expansion: Pace Digitek is in an active manufacturing scale-up. BESS manufacturing capacity of 2.5 GWh was commissioned and operational during FY2026, and a staged expansion to 5 GWh and then 10 GWh is described as underway. The Company continued to invest in manufacturing expansion, backward integration, technology platforms and execution capabilities across its telecom and energy infrastructure businesses. Its integrated BESS manufacturing platform combines battery pack assembly, system integration and containerised energy storage solutions, using automated cell-to-module-to-pack manufacturing, and the localisation strategy is progressing towards higher value addition and backward integration across selected components and infrastructure systems to enhance supply-chain visibility, execution control and long-term competitiveness. The manufacturing base comprises 3 manufacturing facilities with telecom energy systems annual installed capacity of 21,590 nos and telecom infrastructure equipment annual installed capacity of 10,944 nos, alongside experience across 8,000+ execution sites. Capacity utilisation is reported at approximately 80%; Lineage Power Private Limited is described as the Material Subsidiary serving as the Group's integrated manufacturing and technology platform for telecom power systems, BESS and power electronics. On asset creation, the Company made significant progress on its first BOO project, the 750 MW / 1,500 MWh MSEDCL Standalone BESS project in Maharashtra, commissioning 480 MWh during the year ahead of the respective Commercial Operation Dates under a 12-year BOO model; following that commissioning and its accounting recognition, finance lease receivables of Rs. 5,315 Million were recognised. Total equity increased to Rs. 22,522 Million from Rs. 12,090 Million reflecting the IPO and retained earnings, which the Company says strengthens the capital base for investments across manufacturing expansion, project execution capabilities and long-term growth; leverage increased primarily to support manufacturing capacity expansion, integrated project execution, energy asset creation and working capital, while a comfortable leverage profile was maintained. Working capital requirements remained elevated in line with higher EPC execution, manufacturing operations and inventory build-up, with improving cash conversion efficiency, strengthening collections and maintaining balance sheet flexibility named as key management priorities. In the BRSR, 100% of capex investment in both FY 2025-2026 and FY 2024-2025 is stated to be directed towards technologies and infrastructure enabling renewable energy integration and reducing the carbon intensity of energy consumed. No rupee capex quantum is disclosed in this bundle: the capital commitments note arrived only as note headings with no figures, so capex_disclosed is correctly empty.

risks.risk: Input dependence on lithium cells, electronic components and imported inputs
risks.note: The BRSR names responsible supply chain and critical mineral sourcing as a material risk: dependence on lithium cells, electronic components and imported inputs exposes the Company to price volatility, supply disruption and ESG risks within the upstream value chain. It flags this as an input-cost and availability risk, mitigated by diversifying the supplier base, increasing local sourcing aligned with Make-in-India, screening suppliers on ESG parameters and prudent inventory planning. For a business whose growth engine is BESS manufacturing, the cell is the single largest bought-in input, so cost and availability flow straight into project margins.

risks.risk: Occupational health and safety exposure across tower erection, electrical and EPC work
risks.note: Tower erection, electrical work, EPC activities and manufacturing involve work-at-height, electrical and material-handling hazards, and incidents can cause harm to people, project downtime and liability. Mitigation runs through safety management systems, regular training, PPE, permit-to-work procedures, periodic audits and contractor safety governance. Because execution is multi-site and largely contractor-mediated, safety failures translate directly into schedule slippage and claims.

risks.risk: Battery and e-waste product stewardship and Extended Producer Responsibility obligations
risks.note: Lithium-ion batteries and electronic products require safe handling, recycling and disposal under the Battery Waste and E-Waste Management Rules, and the BRSR states that inadequate end-of-life management carries regulatory and reputational risk, with penalties and take-back costs if unmanaged. The mitigation is designing products for recyclability, complying with EPR obligations, partnering with authorised recyclers and tracking end-of-life recovery. This is a durable liability that scales with every GWh shipped.

risks.risk: Governance, anti-bribery and compliance exposure tied to public-sector customers and tender access
risks.note: The BRSR flags that operating across multiple geographies and serving public-sector clients demands high standards of governance, anti-bribery and compliance, and that lapses risk penalties and disqualification from tenders. Since the order book is dominated by central and state agency contracts, a compliance breach is not just a fine but a loss of access to the Company's primary demand channel. Mitigation is via the code of conduct, board oversight, anti-corruption policies, a whistle-blower mechanism and continuous compliance monitoring.

risks.risk: Rising energy and climate-compliance costs from an emissions-intensive manufacturing and execution footprint
risks.note: Manufacturing of power systems and BESS, energy-intensive project execution and operation of telecom infrastructure result in Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions, and the BRSR states that tightening climate regulation, carbon pricing and customer decarbonisation expectations could raise energy and compliance costs. Mitigation is improving energy efficiency at manufacturing facilities, increasing the share of renewable (solar) power, solarising telecom sites and monitoring emission intensity.

risks.risk: Safety and evolving regulatory standards specific to BESS manufacturing and deployment
risks.note: The Company's own HSE Vision 2026 and 2026 BESS HSE roadmap treat BESS safety as a distinct programme, with milestones covering NFPA-compliant fire suppression systems, ISO 45001 and 14001 accreditation, a BESS HSE policy framework and 'zero non-compliance: full alignment with 2026 BESS regulatory statutes'. The framing implies that BESS-specific regulatory statutes and fire-safety expectations are still tightening, and that compliance requires ongoing resource commitment across a rapidly expanding fleet.

risks.risk: Macro and geopolitical exposure across trade and energy corridors feeding an import-dependent input base
risks.note: The MD&A economy overview describes a year in which the global economy had to demonstrate resilience despite rising trade tensions, geopolitical uncertainties and disruptions across key energy corridors. Read alongside the BRSR's stated dependence on lithium cells, electronic components and imported inputs, corridor and trade disruption is the transmission channel through which macro stress reaches the Company's input cost and delivery schedules.

risks.risk: Execution and technology complexity concentrated in a business still scaling its capability base
risks.note: The material-issue table treats the clean-energy and storage transition as the Company's major source of order inflows, with the mitigation being to expand BESS manufacturing capacity, strengthen integrated cell-to-container capabilities and grow the renewable and EPC order book. That concentrates the growth case on delivering a capacity and capability build-out on schedule; the same table's risk rows (supply chain, safety, waste, compliance) are each capable of interrupting that build-out.

themes.title: Renewable IPP / FDRE firm-power & storage
themes.need: DISCOMs mandating firm/round-the-clock RE make BESS + pumped-hydro the bid differentiator, and in Q1FY27 storage demand ran ahead of supply. ADANIGREEN has 3.5 GWh of BESS installed (+1.9 GWh at Khavda this quarter), targets 10+ GWh this fiscal and 50 GWh by FY30 on a thumb-rule INR 25-30 lakh of EBITDA per MWh against ~INR 1.5cr/MWh of capex, and has contracted essentially all merchant/C&I capacity to sibling AESL on 25-year (solar/wind) and 15-year (battery) fixed-price PPAs targeting ~15-16% IRR - a pivot from merchant builder to fixed-return contracted IPP, with evacuation (not panels) named as the binding constraint. JSWENERGY added 873 MW in Q1 and ~1.1 GW since April - 36% of its 3 GW FY27 target already banked, Tidong Hydro commissioned four months early - and raised INR 10,150cr, taking net leverage 5.2x to 4.95x. On the equipment side SERVOTECH said its BESS pack capacity is fully booked ('we are not able to meet the demand') and committed to 2x capacity in 6 months, 3x by 21-Mar-2027 and 10x within 2 years. ACMESOLAR/KPIGREEN/SUZLON/INOXWIND attach storage to solar/wind; NTPC/NHPC/SJVN/TATAPOWER drive pumped-hydro and utility-scale storage.
themes.driver: BESS capacity commissioning against demand two independent managements (ADANIGREEN, SERVOTECH) say already exceeds supply; FDRE/peak-power tender awards; merchant DAM prices (JSWENERGY: INR 4.40 -> INR 5.10/unit, +16%) on +8.5% Q1 power demand.

themes.title: Telecom & digital-infrastructure capex

- Energy EPC projects: MAHAGENCO Solar EPC 200 MW AC (Rs 9,200 Million); Bondada Engineering solar Balance of System works for a 300 MW AC solar power project (Rs 3,340 Million); SECI Standalone BESS 600 MW/1200 MWh (Rs 11,593 Million, 1.20 GWh); NTPC Standalone BESS 200 MW/400 MWh (Rs 5,836 Million, 0.40 GWh); NLC India Standalone BESS 250 MW/500 MWh (Rs 7,099 Million, 0.50 GWh); DVC Standalone BESS 250 MW/500 MWh (Rs 7,020 Million, 0.50 GWh).

margins.title: Margins & cost
margins.body:
- Energy EBITDA margins structurally lower than telecom → blended FY26 EBITDA fell to Rs.455 cr (margin ~17.2%) despite revenue growth.
- Cell cost = 60–65% of container cost. Current container realization $82–84/kWh; cell cost elevated $48–50/kWh (~60% of system value).
- Cell prices +~20% from 1-Apr (China rebate reversal 9%→6%, expiring next yr); inventory pre-stocked protects Q1 FY27; bids carry contingency for rate increases (margin protection). Expect prices to ease from next quarter.
- In-house container fabrication: ~4–5% pricing/operating efficiency gain (imports carry ~30% overhead/freight).
- Employee expense FY26 Rs.96 cr vs Rs.67 cr (energy diversification, project deployment, plant commissioning).

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation (IPO proceeds)
capital_allocation.body:
- IPO funded deleveraging (finance cost halved; rating BBB− → A−) and BESS capacity expansion.
- 4 BOO projects: first three funded via IPO funds / internal accruals; fourth via external resources. **No further BOO projects unless external investment secured** — FY27/28 strategy pivots to product (BESS sales to external customers), not balance-sheet-heavy BOO.
- BOO SPV IRR ~12–13%; parent books separate arm's-length EPC margin (with associated extra tax). MSEDCL revenue model: Rs.2,19,000/MW/month (paid on MW not MWh; e.g. 1,500 MWh ≈ 750 MW).

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Pace Digitek is in an active manufacturing scale-up. BESS manufacturing capacity of 2.5 GWh was commissioned and operational during FY2026, and a staged expansion to 5 GWh and then 10 GWh is described as underway. The Company continued to invest in manufacturing expansion, backward integration, technology platforms and execution capabilities across its telecom and energy infrastructure businesses. Its integrated BESS manufacturing platform combines battery pack assembly, system integration and containerised energy storage solutions, using automated cell-to-module-to-pack manufacturing, and the localisation strategy is progressing towards higher value addition and backward integration across selected components and infrastructure systems to enhance supply-chain visibility, execution control and long-term competitiveness. The manufacturing base comprises 3 manufacturing facilities with telecom energy systems annual installed capacity of 21,590 nos and telecom infrastructure equipment annual installed capacity of 10,944 nos, alongside experience across 8,000+ execution sites. Capacity utilisation is reported at approximately 80%; Lineage Power Private Limited is described as the Material Subsidiary serving as the Group's integrated manufacturing and technology platform for telecom power systems, BESS and power electronics. On asset creation, the Company made significant progress on its first BOO project, the 750 MW / 1,500 MWh MSEDCL Standalone BESS project in Maharashtra, commissioning 480 MWh during the year ahead of the respective Commercial Operation Dates under a 12-year BOO model; following that commissioning and its accounting recognition, finance lease receivables of Rs. 5,315 Million were recognised. Total equity increased to Rs. 22,522 Million from Rs. 12,090 Million reflecting the IPO and retained earnings, which the Company says strengthens the capital base for investments across manufacturing expansion, project execution capabilities and long-term growth; leverage increased primarily to support manufacturing capacity expansion, integrated project execution, energy asset creation and working capital, while a comfortable leverage profile was maintained. Working capital requirements remained elevated in line with higher EPC execution, manufacturing operations and inventory build-up, with improving cash conversion efficiency, strengthening collections and maintaining balance sheet flexibility named as key management priorities. In the BRSR, 100% of capex investment in both FY 2025-2026 and FY 2024-2025 is stated to be directed towards technologies and infrastructure enabling renewable energy integration and reducing the carbon intensity of energy consumed. No rupee capex quantum is disclosed in this bundle: the capital commitments note arrived only as note headings with no figures, so capex_disclosed is correctly empty.

management_tone.title: Management tone
management_tone.body: Confident, ahead-of-plan (advanced 5→10 GWh on demand visibility), claims market leadership (largest standalone BESS order book in India). Candid on margin dilution from energy mix and on working-capital stretch; transparent on cell-cost inflation and mitigation. Slightly evasive/deferring on the repeated receivables-reconciliation questions ("email me separately").

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Integrated business model with end-to-end capabilities spanning manufacturing, EPC execution, system integration and O&M across both telecom and energy infrastructure - the Company describes an integrated value chain running from design and engineering through product development and manufacturing to EPC execution and O&M
- In-house manufacturing backbone through Material Subsidiary Lineage Power Private Limited, enabling better quality control, production consistency and supply chain reliability; automated cell-to-module-to-pack manufacturing supported by rigorous testing and quality assurance
- Backward integration and localisation across selected components and infrastructure systems, including in-house container fabrication, to improve execution control, supply visibility and cost optimisation
- Technology heritage from the 2014 acquisition of the business of GE Power Electronics India and the rights to the Lineage Power brand, which strengthened DC power system capabilities for telecom tower companies and network operators
- 18+ years of operating experience with a proven large-scale, multi-location execution record, including the successfully executed BSNL 4G Saturation project and experience across 8,000+ sites
- Well-established vendor ecosystem and robust supply chain network supporting timely delivery on complex, multi-location projects
- Recurring-revenue engine from a BOO asset platform and long-term O&M components, providing annuity-linked visibility alongside execution-based EPC revenue
- Marquee central and state agency customer base (MSEDCL, KPTCL, KREDL, SECI, NTPC, MAHAGENCO) alongside private-sector engagements, spanning utility-scale and C&I segments
- Continued investments in digital systems, process automation and Management Information Systems (MIS) strengthening operational visibility, execution control and scalability
- Strengthened capital base and financial flexibility following the October 2025 IPO and listing on BSE and NSE

risks.title: Risks
risks.body:
- **Working capital intensity:** trade receivables Rs.2,442 cr (current Rs.1,565 cr); receivables +56% YoY vs revenue +8.3%; payables +77% YoY. Q4-concentrated sales (90–120 day collection). Net debtor-creditor ~Rs.650 cr (~90-day cycle). ~Rs.300 cr collected Apr–May; ease expected by Sep-2026. ~5% retention; ~Rs.900 cr telecom milestone unbilled (3–5 yrs).
- **Input cost / FX:** lithium cell prices +20%, USD exposure; partially hedged via inventory + bid contingencies.
- **Execution / commissioning:** geopolitical shipping disruption already delayed plant ~2 months; project timelines may slip (force majeure invoked sector-wide).
- **Margin dilution:** rising energy mix lowers blended margins.
- **Leverage:** total debt rose Rs.161cr→Rs.961cr (though net D/E low at 0.09x); BOO funding reliance.
- **Receivable reclassification confusion:** investors flagged ~Rs.300–399 cr unexplained gaps vs RHP/annual report (mgmt deferred to email clarification — watch item).
- **Competition:** many players announcing BESS assembly capacity in H2 — mgmt leans on ecosystem (PCS/EMS, 200 field engineers, NOC, ~1.5yr field track record) as moat.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- Telecom (55% of revenue) is the higher-margin cash engine subsidizing the energy growth pivot — the "telecom infra" label undersells its current P&L role.
- BOO is being deliberately capped (only 4 projects, no more without external capital) — strategic shift to asset-light product/EPC model. This is a notable de-risking vs typical BESS developer playbooks.
- Cell manufacturing entry "announcement soon" = potential major capex/strategy catalyst not yet in numbers.
- ~Rs.900 cr telecom receivables are unbilled milestone (3–5 yr horizon) — a chunk of "receivables" is contractual future billing, softening the WC-scare optics.
- Force majeure / 2–4 month project extension provisions sector-wide could shift FY27 revenue recognition timing.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:

Both are quoted as printed; the deck does not reconcile them.

- [Guidance] Management gives revenue guidance of FY27E Rs. 32,000-34,000 mn and FY28E Rs. 40,000-42,000 mn (a forward-looking statement subject to the deck's disclaimer).
